nahhas-irab:1-2.t: الرَّحْمنُ (1): nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ (2), i.e. out of His mercy He taught the Qur'an, and by it He made clear His good pleasure, which brings one near to Him, and His displeasure, which drives one away from Him and from His mercy.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t: So it is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). It was said: the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. they both run بِحُسْبانٍ. And it was said: the khabar is بِحُسْبانٍ.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: النجم is whatever crops spread out over the ground, meaning herbs and the like; he said: and الشجر is whatever stands on a stem. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best of what has been said about its meaning, i.e. everything prostrates to Him, i.e. submits to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَالسَّماءَ رَفَعَها: You put it in the accusative by an implied verb, conjoining what a verb governed onto its like. وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزانَ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. justice. Someone else said: it is the balance with which things are weighed.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزانِ (8): «أن» is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "so that you do not transgress" (بأن لا تطغوا); تَطْغَوْا is in the position of the accusative by أن. It is also possible for «أن» to have the meaning of أي (i.e. explicative), in which case it has no grammatical position, and تطغوا is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is preferable, because after it comes وَأَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلا تُخْسِرُوا الْمِيزانَ (9). Bilāl ibn Abī Burda read وَلا تُخْسِرُوا with fatḥa on the tāʾ [i.e. تَخسَروا]; it is a well-known dialect.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: الأرض is in the accusative by an implied verb.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: فِيها فاكِهَةٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). وَالنَّخْلُ ذاتُ الْأَكْمامِ: conjoined to it. The singular is كمّ, which is whatever surrounds it [the fruit] of fibre, palm fronds and other things.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَالْحَبُّ: nominative as being conjoined to فاكهة, i.e. "and in it are grains." ذُو الْعَصْفِ: a naʿt (adjective) of it. وَالرَّيْحانُ: also conjoined. The reading of al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحانُ in the genitive [i.e. والريحانِ], in the sense of "and possessing fragrant herbs" (وذو الريحان).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: [it means] "So which of the blessings of your Lord [will you both deny]?" Abū Jaʿfar said: If it is said: only man has been mentioned before, so how does the address come to be to two things? There is more than one answer to this. Among them: الأنام includes the jinn and mankind, so they were addressed on that basis. It was also said: when He, Majestic and Mighty, said وَالْجَانَّ خَلَقْناهُ [al-Ḥijr: 27], and man had been mentioned before, all were addressed. al-Farrāʾ permitted that it be an address to a single person using the verb of two, and he reported that from the Arabs.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: الصّلصال is dry clay. On this view the meaning is: He created man from dry clay that makes a sound as clay sounds when fire has touched it, and that is earthenware (al-fakhkhār). It was also said: الصلصال means "stinking", of the pattern faʿlāl, from صلّ اللحم when meat becomes putrid; one also says أصلّ.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t: It was said: المارج is derived from مرج الشيء when a thing becomes mixed; المارج is from between yellow, green and red, and so is the tongue of fire. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on مِنْ مارِجٍ مِنْ نارٍ; he said: it is from the pure [part] of fire.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); it may be a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in «خلق». The genitive is permissible, meaning: "So which of the blessings of your Lord, Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests…", and the accusative is permissible in the sense of "I mean" (أعني).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: It is not repetition, because it only comes after blessings other than those that preceded.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: مرج means "He released." The scholars disagreed about the meaning of "the two seas" here. al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: they are the sea of the Byzantines (the Mediterranean) and the sea of Persia. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abzā said: they are the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth; the like is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, except that he said: they meet every year. The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abzā is the one Muḥammad ibn Jarīr adopts, for a reason that made it necessary in his view, which we will mention after this.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: Some of the people of tafsīr said: they do not transgress against people. Some of them said: neither of them transgresses against the other. The apparent sense of the verse indicates generality.

nahhas-irab:22-23.t:
The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza is يَخْرُجُ [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant has been lost in the printed text; the reading meant is with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. يُخرَج, "is brought out", as the next sentence shows], and the ḍamma is clearer, because it only comes out when it is brought out.

The scholars discussed the meaning of يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ. The position of al-Farrāʾ is that it only comes out of one of them, and he treated it as figurative. The remoteness in taking «منهما» to mean "from one of them" is not hidden from anyone with understanding. It was also said: يخرج is only for the future, so he says: it will come out of both of them after this. It was also said: it comes out of both of them literally, not figuratively, because it only comes out of the places where the salt water and the fresh water meet. A fourth view is the one Muḥammad ibn Jarīr chose. What led him to it was the tafsīr: someone whose word is taken as proof had said about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيانِ that they are the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth, and pearls and coral are only found in shells when rain falls on them. What shows you this is the ḥadīth from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: "When the sky rains, the shells open their mouths."

nahhas-irab:24-25.t:
الجواري is in the position of the nominative; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. Dropping the yāʾ [in writing/pronunciation] is far-fetched; whoever drops the yāʾ says the kasra indicates it, and it used to be dropped before the alif and lām were added.

The reading of the Kufans, except al-Kisāʾī, is وَلَهُ الْجَوارِ الْمُنْشِئاتُ [i.e. with kasra on the shīn], making them [the ships] the agents; «المنشأات» [with fatḥa] is the reading of the people of Medina and of Abū ʿAmr, and it is clearer. As for what is related from ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, that he read المنشيّات, it is not reliably preserved, because if he replaced the hamza he would say المنشيات, and if he lightened it he would make it between alif and hamza and say المنشاءات, and this is what is preserved of his reading. كالأعلام is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). [Translator's note: the printed text has «كالأعلم».]

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
The pronoun refers back to the earth, which He placed [Translator's note: i.e. mentioned earlier in وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَها]; i.e. everyone on the earth passes away and perishes.
The origin is فاني; the vowel on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was made vowelless, then it was dropped because of its vowellessness and the vowellessness of the tanwīn after it.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: ذُو is a naʿt (adjective) of وجه, because the meaning is "and your Lord remains," as you say: "this is the face of the earth." In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd [it is] ويبقى وجه ربك ذي الجلال والإكرام, as a naʿt of ربّك.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: يَسْئَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: The position of Qatāda — not in his exact words — is: the people of the heavens and the people of the earth turn to Him in their needs; they cannot do without Him. كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ: i.e. concerned with their affairs, their well-being and the management of their matters.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: There are five readings of it. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned two of them, each of which was read by five readers: they are (سنفرغ) and (سيفرغ). The first was read by Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read (سيفرغ) — Abū ʿUbayd did not mention Ṭalḥa. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj and Qatāda read (سنفرغ لكم) with fatḥa on the nūn and the rāʾ. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (سنفرغ) with kasra on the nūn and fatḥa on the rāʾ, and al-Farrāʾ mentioned that it is read (سيفرغ) with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first two readings have one meaning. Abū ʿUbayd reported that the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and Tihāma is فرغ يفرغ and that the dialect of the people of Najd is فرغ يفرغ [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing the two dialects has been lost in the printed text; presumably faragha yafrughu versus fariġa/faragha yafragu], and that he knew of no one among the readers who read according to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned who read according to it. Whoever says فرغ يفرغ [with fatḥa in the imperfect] brings it according to the original pattern, because it contains one of the guttural letters — the guttural letters are hamza, ʿayn, ghayn, ḥāʾ, khāʾ and hāʾ — and from the guttural letters the pattern faʿala yafʿalu comes frequently, such as ذهب يذهب and صنع يصنع; and there come [verbs] with two dialects, such as صبغ يصبغ and يصبغ, and رعف يرعف and يرعف; and from them there come [verbs] that are hardly ever given fatḥa, such as نحت ينحت. In this one only goes back to [actual] usage.

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: يا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ: a vocative in construct. إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطارِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا: According to the position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the meaning is: "We shall attend to you, O you two weighty ones," and it will be said to you: "O company of jinn and men." He mentioned that this is on the Day of Resurrection: the angels of the seven heavens will descend and surround the regions of the earth, then the Highest King, Majestic and Mighty, will come. al-Ḍaḥḥāk recited: وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا [al-Fajr: 22]. Then Hell will be brought, and when people see it they will flee, while the angels have lined up along the regions of the earth in seven rows. al-Ḍaḥḥāk recited: يَوْمَ التَّنادِ يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ [Ghāfir: 32, 33], and recited: إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطارِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا. It is related from him that he said: "If you are able to flee from death." It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "If you are able to know what is in the heavens and what is in the earth." لا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطانٍ: ʿIkrima said: i.e. by a proof; he said: every سلطان in the Qur'an means a proof. Qatāda said: بسلطان, i.e. by dominion.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُما شُواظٌ مِنْ نارٍ: This is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read — and it is related from al-Ḥasan — (شواظ) with kasra on the shīn. al-Farrāʾ holds that they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says صوار and صوار [i.e. ṣuwār and ṣiwār]. (ونحاس) is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and the Kufans in the nominative; Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr read (ونحاس) in the genitive; Mujāhid read (ونحاس) with kasra on the nūn and the sīn [i.e. ونِحاسٍ]; and Muslim ibn Jundab read (ونحس) without alif and in the nominative.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The nominative in «ونحاس» is clearer in Arabic, because there is no difficulty in it: it is conjoined to «شواظ». If you put it in the genitive, you conjoin it to نار, and you need a contrivance. That is because most of the people of tafsīr, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, say: الشّواظ is the flame and النحاس is the smoke. So if you put it in the genitive, the implied form is "a flame of fire and of smoke," and a flame is not of smoke, just as a blaze is not of smoke, except by a contrivance and an excuse. The contrivance in that — and it is the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] — is that since the flame and the smoke are both from the fire, each of them comprises the other. He recited [a verse] of al-Farazdaq: [ṭawīl metre] 447-
فبتّ أقدّ الزاد بيني وبينه ... على ضوء نار مرّة ودخان
(I spent the night cutting the provisions between me and him [the wolf], by the light of a fire at times, and of smoke.)
So he conjoined ودخان to نار, though smoke has no light, because light and smoke [both] come from the fire; and if you conjoin ودخان to ضوء you do not need a contrivance. Someone else recited on exactly this point: [rajaz metre] 448-
شراب ألبان وتمر وأقط
(A drinker of milk, and dates, and dried curd.)
Only the milk is drunk, but the throat comprises these things. Another said similarly: [majzūʾ al-kāmil metre] 449-
يا ليت زوجك قد غدا ... متقلّدا سيفا ورمحا
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning girded with a sword and a spear.)
— because both are carried. al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَنُحاسٌ: the copper (al-nuḥās) will be melted and poured on their heads. فَلا تَنْتَصِرانِ: i.e. against whoever punishes you both with that, nor will you gain help from Him [Translator's note: or "against Him"].

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: i.e. So which of the blessings of your Lord — who made the ruling one and the same in preventing [anyone] from passing through, and did not single out anyone in it to the exclusion of another — [will you deny]? [Translator's note: the printed text has «النقود» (coins), apparently for «النفوذ» (passing through); translated according to the context.]

nahhas-irab:37-38.t: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ: and that is the Day of Resurrection. فَكانَتْ وَرْدَةً: Qatāda said: today it is green, and on the Day of Resurrection red. Someone else added: and it is of iron. كَالدِّهانِ: The soundest thing said about it — and it is the view of Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk — is that it is the plural of دهن (oil), i.e. clear and smooth.

nahhas-irab:39-42.t: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ: the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا. لا يُسْئَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلا جَانٌّ: The view of Ibn ʿAbbās: they are not asked a question for finding out, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has kept a record of their deeds against them. The view of Qatāda: they are known by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes; what indicates this is that after it comes يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيماهُمْ. السيما and السيمياء mean a mark. فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي وَالْأَقْدامِ: بالنواصي may be in the position of the nominative as the noun whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and it may be implied [i.e. the deputy agent is an implied pronoun].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: i.e. it will be said to them: this is Hell, which they used to deny in the world.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها: i.e. between its layers. وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb reported from Ibn Zayd; he said: الآني means "present." Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on بَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ; he said: He is saying: its heat has reached its extreme. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is so in the speech of the Arabs; al-Nābigha said: [wāfir metre] 450-
وتخضب لحية غدرت وخانت ... بأحمر من نجيع الجوف ان
(And she dyes a beard that was treacherous and betrayed, with a red [flow] of the belly's blood, at its utmost heat.)

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: i.e. So which of the blessings of your Lord, which He bestowed on you — for He punished none of you but the criminals, and gave them a mark by which they are known so that others are not mixed up with them — [will you deny]?

nahhas-irab:46-47.t: Nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and by an implied verb meaning "is due" or "is established." The implied construction is: "and for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, so performs His obligations and avoids disobeying Him out of fear of the standing at which Allah the Exalted will make him stand for the reckoning." What makes this clear is His saying: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى [al-Nāziʿāt: 40]; and one who plunges into acts of disobedience is not called "fearful." Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on وَلِمَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ; he said: Allah has promised the believers who performed His obligations the Garden.

nahhas-irab:48-49.t: A naʿt (adjective) of the two gardens. al-janna among the Arabs is the orchard. Abū Jaʿfar said: The singular of الأفنان is فنن according to whoever says they are the branches; whoever says they are the kinds — the kinds of fruit — [says] its singular, in their view, is فن. The first is more likely to be correct, because فنّ is mostly pluralised as فنون, so its plural of multitude suffices, just as one says شسع and شسوع. From it is taken [the expression] "so-and-so went into various kinds (funūn) of talk."

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: i.e. among them are two flowing rivers.

nahhas-irab:52-53.t: i.e. of every kind of fruit there are two varieties.

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: مُتَّكِئِينَ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is among the obscure points of grammar. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no one among the grammarians who mentioned it, except something Muḥammad ibn Jarīr mentioned; he said: it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. they enjoy themselves reclining, and he made what precedes it indicate the omitted [verb]. Abū Jaʿfar said: It may be without any omission, referring back to His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَلِمَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ, as you say: لفلان تجارة حاضرا ("so-and-so has trade while present"), i.e. in this state. مُتَّكِئِينَ is according to the meaning of «من»; had it been according to the wording it would have been متّكئا. وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); دانٍ is its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:56-57.t: فِيهِنَّ: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned this pronoun and to whom it refers; there is a difficulty in it, which we have explained. The implied construction is: in them are ḥūr. قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلا جَانٌّ; and the reading of Ṭalḥa is لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing Ṭalḥa's variant has been lost in the printed text; presumably يطمُثهنّ with ḍamma on the mīm]; they are two well-known dialects.

nahhas-irab:58-59.t: أن is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the kāf is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being omitted. «هنّ» is in the position of the accusative as the noun of «أنّ», and it was doubled because it is equivalent to two letters in the masculine [i.e. هم]. الْياقُوتُ is the khabar, and وَالْمَرْجانُ is conjoined to it. [Translator's note: the printed text has «عطل» for «عطف».]

nahhas-irab:60-61.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); i.e. [what is] the reward of one who did good in the world, except that good be done to him in the Hereafter?

nahhas-irab:62-63.t: There are two views on its meaning. One of them: "and below them two" in rank (degrees). This is the position of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he interpreted these two gardens [the first two] as being the ones about which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ [al-Sajda: 17]. The other view is: "and below them two" in excellence; this is the position of Ibn Zayd; he said: and they are for the Companions of the Right.

nahhas-irab:64-65.t: Abū Ḥātim said: مدهمّتان is permissible in ordinary speech, because one says ادهمّ and ادهامّ. مدهامتان is a naʿt (adjective) of the two gardens.

nahhas-irab:66-67.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on [نَ]ضَّاخَتانِ [Translator's note: the printed text has «ضَّاخَتانِ» with the initial nūn missing]; he said: "overflowing." al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "full." Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: gushing with water and fruit. Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known in the language is that they [gush] with water.

nahhas-irab:68-69.t: There are three views about it. Among them: it was said that palm trees and pomegranates are not among the fruits, since in this verse they are set apart from them. It was also said: they are among them, but they were mentioned again in praise of them, because of their excellence. It was also said: the Arabs repeat a thing with the wāw of conjunction for amplitude, not for preference, and the Qur'an came down in their language. The evidence for that is أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ [al-Ḥajj: 18], then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ; and He, exalted be His praise, said: حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ وَالصَّلاةِ الْوُسْطى [al-Baqara: 238]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is clear; there is no ambiguity in it.

nahhas-irab:70-71.t: al-Farrāʾ reported خيّرات and خيرات. As for the Basrans, they said: خيرة has the meaning of خيّرة, and it was lightened, just as one says ميّت and ميت. «فيهن» refers back to the four gardens.

nahhas-irab:72-73.t: حُورٌ: a badal (substitute), or if you wish, a naʿt (adjective). مَقْصُوراتٌ: Mujāhid said: they have restricted their glances and themselves to their husbands, and do not want others. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: «مقصورات» means confined. al-Ḥasan said: مقصورات means confined, not going about in the streets. Abū Jaʿfar said: What is correct in this is to say: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described them as مقصورات and made it general, so we make it general as He, Majestic and Mighty, made it general, and say: they have restricted their glances and themselves to their husbands, so they do not see others, and they are confined in the pavilions and guarded.

nahhas-irab:74-75.t: So by this He indicated that the jinn have intercourse.

nahhas-irab:76-77.t:
مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ: خضر is the plural of أخضر, and رفرف is singular in form, but it has been described with a plural because it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), as one says: مررت برهط كرام وقوم لئام ("I passed by a noble band and a base people"), and likewise هذه إبل حسان وغنم صغار ("these are fine camels and small sheep"). وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ is like it, except that it may be the plural of عبقرية. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read متكئين على رفارف خضر وعباقريّ حسان, and some related this reading from ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī from Abū Bakra from the Prophet ﷺ, but its isnad (chain of transmission) is not sound. Abū ʿUbayd claimed that if it were sound it would be وعباقريَّ without full declension (ijrāʾ), and claimed that this is what Arabic requires.

Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear error in the view of all the grammarians, because they have all agreed that one says رجل مدائنيّ ("a man of al-Madāʾin") with full declension; he only imagined that it is a plural. There is in the speech of the Arabs no plural having four letters after its alif. There is no disagreement among them that if you pluralised عبقر you would say عباقر, and, far-fetchedly, عباقير, and عباقرة is permissible. As for عباقريّ as a plural, it is impossible. The reason why عباقريّ cannot be permitted is that it must either be a relative adjective (nisba) of عبقر, in which case one says عبقريّ, or a relative adjective of عباقر, in which case it is returned to the singular and one also says عبقريّ — as all the grammarians laid down regarding the nisba of a plural, that you form the nisba from its singular, so you say for the nisba of المساجد: مسجديّ, of العلوم: علميّ, and of الفرائض: فرضيّ. If someone says: what prevents عباقر from being the name of a place to which the nisba is then formed, as one says معافريّ? It is said to him: the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is not construed according to what is not known, while abandoning the proof of consensus.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t:
تَبارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ: i.e. blessing is in His name, Majestic and Mighty. Blessing (al-baraka) in the language is the permanence and firmness of a favour.
So by this He urged them to mention His name, Majestic and Mighty, often, and to call upon Him, and to mention Him with reverence and glorification of Him, so He said: ذي الجلل والإكرام [Translator's note: so in the printed text, for ذِي الْجَلالِ], i.e. the Majestic, the Noble. In the ḥadīth: «ألظّوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام» ("Hold fast to [saying] 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honour'").
